{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABf9g4bw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhJabZA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 108, "title": "Remove the bundled demo game and make the web player user-ROM-only", "body": "## Problem

The web player still bundles and promotes the original **Beacon Trail** demo game. The user no longer wants any demo game or built-in playable cartridge: **remove it completely**, including its ROM binary, source/build pipeline, download links, UI entry points, demo-specific tests, and active documentation.

The player should instead open empty and let the user **select their own local WonderSwan ROM**. There must be no automatic ROM loading, bundled downloadable game, "Play demo" option or special-case code for the removed game. Backwards compatibility with the removed demo is **not** required.

This is a focused removal / simplification task, not a request to add a ROM catalog, fetch games online, or weaken emulator hardware functionality.

## Expected outcome

- After initialization, the empty player presents a clear, prominent **Load ROM** action and a concise indication that a local `.ws` / `.wsc` file is required. No cartridge is preloaded; normal gameplay starts only after a user selects a file.
- The ROM is read locally using the existing file picker; no game files are supplied, downloaded, fetched automatically, uploaded to a server, or bundled into the deployable site. Do not imply the application verifies ownership: users choose ROM files they are entitled to use.
- No Beacon Trail/demo content, source, binary, buttons, help text, download links or obsolete build steps remain in the maintained application/repository. **Independent original CC0 hardware compatibility fixtures are not a bundled demo** and should remain available for development tests under `fixtures/`, but must not be published as a ready-to-play built-in ROM.
- Existing user-supplied-ROM features continue to work: three console models, cartridge validation, pause/resume/restart, controls, display effects, audio, browser saves/console EEPROM/RTC, Debug Mode and errors. Do not spend effort preserving the deleted demo's gameplay, win state, visuals or tests.

## Context and reproduction

The current `main` has these concrete dependencies to remove or revise:

- [`web/public/demo/`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/tree/main/web/public/demo) contains the **publicly shipped** `beacon-trail.ws` and `NOTICE.txt`. Delete this directory; the Vite production build must not include a playable ROM.
- [`demo/`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/tree/main/demo) contains `game.asm`, `graphics.py`, `build.py`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`. Remove the demo-specific directory, including build/provenance assets that no longer serve a maintained purpose.
- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) has `#demo` in the empty state, `#demo-again` in Settings / Help, a game-specific introduction, the demo download/source/license links, and references to a silent demo. Replace these with short **local-ROM-only** guidance. Keep essential instructions for controls, display effects, mute and storage, but do not introduce a new help page or unnecessary UI.
- [`web/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/src/main.ts) wires `demoButton`, `playDemo()`, the network fetch to `demo/beacon-trail.ws`, `demoAfterDialog` and demo-specific async/error paths. Remove all of them and any stale DOM references. Keep the existing local-file load path, proper sound unlock on a trusted user action, safe async load races and clean model/ROM lifecycle.
- [`crates/ws-core/tests/demo.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/crates/ws-core/tests/demo.rs) checks the deleted game. Remove it and any other `include_bytes!` or production/test code depending specifically on the deleted ROM. Do not replace these with an equally hard-coded new bundled game.
- [`web/scripts/smoke.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/scripts/smoke.mjs) has extensive Beacon Trail-specific gameplay/win, input, demo fetch, download and async-race assertions; [`web/scripts/compat.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/web/scripts/compat.mjs) tests demo audio activation and silence. **Retain useful generic browser coverage** by testing an existing independent CC0 `fixtures/generated/*.ws` cartridge through the **local file picker** where appropriate, rather than deleting general input/ROM/audio/error/resize/display tests merely because they used the demo.
- [`README.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/README.md) contains demo-focused instructions, commands, provenance, a throughput example using `web/public/demo/beacon-trail.ws`, and post-merge guidance. Update these to describe the **user-file-only** flow; use the existing CC0 fixture path for runnable development examples if needed. Review active build scripts, docs, tests and links for references to deleted paths.
- Maintain the repo's [UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [test/CI performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles). All newly authored development text is in English.

### Scope and boundaries

1. **Delete**, do not hide: remove the game ROM, `demo/` sources, built-in demo URLs, buttons, event handlers, downloads and all obsolete demo-specific test/build code. Verify a search of *active* app and documentation files has no remaining Beacon Trail/demo feature references. Historical closed Issue/PR discussions need not be rewritten; archive-only validation records may be preserved as history, but must not cause broken active documentation links or build/test dependencies.
2. **Simplify the initial experience**: show a neutral blank/placeholder player before file selection and a visible primary `Load ROM` call to action. Avoid both a redundant primary and toolbar button if one clear action suffices. Keep user instructions minimal, correct and accessible. The input accepts local `.ws` and `.wsc`, while existing ROM validation remains in the core.
3. **Local-only loading and error recovery**: a selected cartridge should boot with its model, orientation, saves, audio and visual options. A cancelled file picker should leave the empty/running state intact. Invalid files and failed asynchronous reads should report recoverable errors without downloading an alternate ROM or silently replacing the user's current cartridge. No automatic retry with a bundled example.
4. **Preserve generic test confidence with less obsolete code**: remove assertions for Beacon Trail objectives/graphics/gameplay; replace generic 3-model CPU/Wasm, file-picker, keyboard/touch, dialog, fullscreen, audio activation, failure and state-isolation checks with **targeted existing fixture(s)** or synthetic local files where possible. Retain meaningful tests for user's own ROMs and avoid unnecessary duplicate test suites. Existing independent `fixtures/` source and generated binaries may remain in the repository, but are for **tests and development only** and must not be copied into `web/public`/`web/dist`.
5. **Minimal dependencies**: no new frontend framework, game assets, ROM chooser service, remote content/API, server-side ROM storage, ROM auto-remembering or unrelated Rust emulation changes. Keep CC0 test fixture provenance where it is still used.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Remove all `demo/` project files and `web/public/demo/` assets, including `beacon-trail.ws` and its download notice. No built-in game asset, bundled demo URL, launcher or source code remains in the current product/build.
- [ ] The fresh site has **no loaded ROM**, a clearly discoverable `Load ROM` control, accessible instructions, no demo CTA or demo-specific help/links, and no automatic game/network fetch. A supplied local ROM loads and runs normally. Verify that the final `web/dist` contains no playable ROM binaries.
- [ ] Remove demo-specific `main.ts` branches/DOM references and `crates/ws-core/tests/demo.rs` plus any other direct references to the removed file. Remove/repair stale commands and active documentation links. A source search for `Beacon Trail`, `beacon-trail`, `Play demo`, `demo-again` and deleted asset paths finds no remaining active behavior or broken references.
- [ ] Keep and adapt Playwright smoke/compatibility tests to exercise **local file picker** load, no ROM before selection, invalid file/cancellation, failed load preservation, keyboard/touch/controller input, pause/resume/restart, modal/focus, fullscreen, shader/portrait presentation, sound activation and browser-local saves where relevant. Demo-specific win/score and intentionally silent demo checks are removed, not replaced by an unrelated new game.
- [ ] Verify no ROM or ROM bytes are fetched/uploaded over the network as part of player startup or file selection, and selecting the same locally supplied ROM restores its save according to existing rules. Test-only CC0 fixtures stay source-reproducible and outside the published site.
- [ ] Keep existing independent core unit/integration tests and relevant native, Wasm, Web UI and display tests passing after removal (adjust only tests that actually depend on the deleted game). Run and report applicable `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, and in `web`: `npm ci`, `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run test:compat`. **Do not run or demand the deleted `demo/build.py` check.**
- [ ] Update README, Settings/Help and current workflow/benchmark instructions to accurately reflect **ROMs supplied by users** and the absence of any playable bundled demo. Keep historical Issue/PR records intact and avoid unrelated emulator/UI changes.

## Optional validation

Test manually on a mobile browser with a locally provided, legally redistributable homebrew ROM to confirm the empty-state UI and file-picker affordance. This is optional, not a requirement to obtain a commercial ROM.

## Required post-merge verification

1. **Pending:** After merging and closing the completed Issue, confirm the normal GitHub Pages deploy on `main` succeeds and record its run URL/commit.
2. **Pending:** On the published URL, verify there is no built-in game or demo/download link, the page starts empty, and a user-selected local test fixture runs without uploading the ROM. Report failures as linked follow-ups instead of reopening a completed Issue solely for publication checks.

Do not claim these production checks completed before deployment.
